cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, MA, that operates an AI music generation platform at suno.com. The company describes its service as an AI song generator that can produce complete original songs, including vocals, lyrics, and full production, from a single text prompt in under a minute, across any genre. A free tier is available, while paid plans add higher monthly song limits and additional features: the Pro plan offers 500 songs per month, royalty-free music, commercial use rights, stem separation, audio uploads of up to 8 minutes, and access to what the company calls its best and most personalized model, v5.5. The Premier plan extends that to 2,000 songs per month and includes Suno Studio, which the company describes as a first-of-its-kind web-based generative audio workstation combining traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered creation, along with a multitrack editor, MIDI export, and Persona Voices.

Suno faces substantial litigation tied to its AI training and music generation practices. The most prominent case is UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc., filed in the District of Massachusetts, and several additional suits have been brought in that same district, including cases brought by Rugnetta, Pilavian, Reyna, and S.A. Jamendo. Further actions have been filed in the Southern District of Texas, the Southern District of New York, and the Northern District of Illinois, with the site's records showing 95 distinct legal exposures coded to Massachusetts. The volume and variety of these cases reflect the IP provenance questions the site itself flags in connection with Suno's music generation product.
